history.summary: NOT A HINDU TEMPLE - keep-or-drop decision needed: Khuangchera Puk is a natural cave ('puk' = cave in Mizo), not a temple. CSV TOWN CORRECTION: it is NOT in Champhai - the cave stands at Ailawng near Reiek village, about 30 km west of Aizawl in Mamit district (the grottomap survey lists the Ailawng area in Mamit district); town corrected to Ailawng and district corrected to Mamit. The cave is named after Khuangchera, a legendary Mizo warrior of the late 19th century: his villagers relied on a spring flowing from a narrow cave but superstition kept anyone from entering it, and Khuangchera ventured in with a bamboo torch and proved that the two entrances on opposite sides of the hillside connected through one underground passage beneath the hill (an early-1980s local club later re-explored and documented the cave in his memory). The 150-162 m long tunnel cave is of gravitational origin, developed along a zigzagging rift in mudstone of the Bhuban Formation (Miocene), with two opposite entrances - an upper south-western sinkhole entrance and a lower north-eastern triangular resurgence entrance near the first houses of Ailawng. It is described as Mizoram's second-longest cave (some sources say the longest - verify). It served as a hideout in times of inter-village conflict and is now a tourist attraction for caving and climbing. Foreign tourists require an Inner Line Permit for Mizoram (verify current rules).

name: Khuangchera Puk
town_description: Ailawng is a small village near Reiek, about 30 km west of Aizawl in Mamit district, Mizoram, on the Reiek-Ailawng road at about 1,485 m above sea level. Reiek is a well-known hill station and tourist hub with the Heritage Village and Reiek Tlang (cliff); the two entrances of Khuangchera Puk lie a short walk from the Ailawng road, marked by signboards.
tradition: Mizo folklore/historic landmark - cave, not a Hindu shrine
